name: TESSERACT
notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).

Status 'proposed' (not 'approved' or 'construction'): sources read speak of 'Proposed experiment at LSM' (TAUP 2025 slides) and 'a period of targeted R&D' (IDM 2026 abstract). Slides of an earlier talk say 'Selected for DOE funding starting FY25' (not cited as an interval: the scope of the funding decision is not stated).

SPICE and HeRALD are the experiment's detector technologies; they also have their own records (experiment:spice, experiment:herald) because the collaboration's site calls them 'two experiments'. The third French Ge/Si bolometer module has no record: it is a proposal inside the TESSERACT payload.

Schedules conflict over time: NPB 2024 'first competitive ultra-light DM searches starting in 2026'; LBNL March 2025 'Construction is slated to begin in 2025, with the experiment coming online around 2029'; TAUP 2025 'between 2027 and 2028'; IDM 2026 'full integration ... planned for 2028'. The latest two are recorded as planned intervals.

physics_goals.quote: The future TESSERACT (Transition Edge Sensors with Sub-eV Resolution And Cryogenic Targets) experiment aims at detecting light dark matter, from the proton mass down to a fraction of an electronvolt
physics_goals.value: Search for sub-GeV dark matter, from the proton mass down to a fraction of an electronvolt, through nuclear and electron recoils

summary.plain: TESSERACT is a planned dark matter experiment that uses ultra-sensitive superconducting sensors to look for particles far lighter than a proton. Its detectors are proposed for the deep Modane underground laboratory in the French Alps. A surface prototype at Berkeley has already set new limits.
summary.technical: Proposed multi-target cryogenic experiment for sub-GeV dark matter (nuclear and electron recoils) with transition-edge-sensor athermal-phonon readout: SPICE (Al2O3, SiO2 polar crystals and GaAs scintillator), HeRALD (superfluid 4He) and a proposed French Ge/Si bolometer module, 10 g to 1 kg of each target, aiming at masses down to 10 MeV/c^2. Proposed host: LSM (about 4800 m.w.e.), in the former EDELWEISS-III area, with two similar cryostats. First result: 2025 above-ground limits from a 0.233 g Si detector (44-87 MeV/c^2). Schedule per June 2026: full integration at LSM planned for 2028.
